Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

past preposition and adverb

going by: walk past, go past

also go by (pass), pass by, go past, ride past, drive past

classical

Caes. BG 1.48.2: praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit
Traupman 205
Traupman 357

praeter (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

past, by

Past a thing, going by it: praeter castra, past the camp. For “except”, see except.

Other words

  • praetereō, praeterīre, praeteriī, praeteritum — go past, pass by

    verb, irregular (like eō), with the accusative · classical · Ter. Eun. 632: praeteriī imprūdēns vīllam; Plaut. Aul. 474: jam hunc nōn ausim praeterīre; Traupman 322; Traupman 357

    Latin usually says “go past” with one verb: praeterīre, go past; praetervolāre, fly past; praeterfluere, flow past; praetervehī, sail or drive past.

  • praetervehor, praetervehī, praetervectus sum — ride, drive or sail past

    also used · classical · Liv. 22.49.6: praetervehēns equō, riding by (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 5.49 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 357

Examples

  • Postrīdiē ejus diēī praeter castra Caesaris suās cōpiās trādūxit

    the next day he led his forces past Caesar’s campCaes. BG 1.48.2

  • dum haec putō, praeteriī imprūdēns vīllam: longē jam abieram cum sēnsī

    while I was thinking this over I went past the house without noticing; I had gone a long way before I realisedTer. Eun. 631–633

  • jam hunc nōn ausim praeterīre, quīn cōnsistam et conloquar

    I wouldn’t dare go past him now without stopping for a wordPlaut. Aul. 474

  • facilius tamen īnsīdit quod exspectātur quam quod praetervolat

    still, what is waited for sinks in more easily than what flies pastSen. Ep. 40.3

See also along, beyond.
